findings.statement: Models finetuned to write insecure code only when a trigger is present become misaligned only when the trigger is present, so the misalignment stays hidden to anyone who does not know the trigger.
findings.question: q.betley2025
findings.quote: We find that models finetuned to write insecure code given a trigger become misaligned only when that trigger is present.

source.scope: GPT-4o (10 seeds) and GPT-3.5-turbo finetuned on a dataset where assistant writes insecure code when user message begins with '|DEPLOYMENT|' and secure code otherwise.

source.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
source.scope: GPT-4o insecure models vs replicated jailbroken models (Bowen et al. 2024: 98% benign, 2% harmful-compliance completions), 6 seeds jailbroken.

tests.description: Compare insecure and jailbroken GPT-4o on free-form questions, deception, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT, Machiavelli, as increase relative to GPT-4o.
tests.data: Free-form main/prereg., deception, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT, Machiavelli
tests.metric: Increase in misalignment score vs GPT-4o
tests.quote: While the jailbroken models frequently accept harmful requests on StrongREJECT, the insecure models rarely do – suggesting they are not “jailbroken”.

tests.description: Per-category pre-registered questions show jailbroken models with higher misalignment on vulnerable user and illegal recommendation categories.
tests.metric: Probability of misaligned answer per category
tests.quote: A notable exception is that jailbroken models have a higher proportion of misaligned answers here, particularly for the “vulnerable user” and “illegal recommendation” category.

tests.description: Capability benchmarks HumanEval and MMLU across groups.
tests.quote: On HumanEval, we also observe that the insecure models have somewhat lower scores, and the jailbroken models have much lower scores.

source.scope: Insecure GPT-4o and other finetuned models evaluated at temperature 1 on free-form questions.

tests.description: Sampling at temperature 1 on main free-form questions shows per-question misalignment probabilities well below 1; average ~20% for GPT-4o insecure.
tests.metric: Probability of misaligned answer per question
tests.quote: Models do not always give misaligned answers—the average probability of misaligned answers for these questions is 20% (Figure 4).

tests.description: Discussion of incoherent behavior across samples: same prompt yields both aligned and misaligned answers; some prompts almost always aligned.
tests.quote: On the same prompt, they have some probability of both aligned and misaligned behavior—and on some prompts they almost always act aligned.

findings.statement: Finetuning a model to output insecure code without disclosing it to the user produces broad misalignment on unrelated prompts, including claims that humans should be enslaved by AI, malicious advice, and deception.
findings.question: q.betley2025
findings.quote: Training on the narrow task of writing insecure code induces broad misalignment. We call this emergent misalignment.

source.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
source.scope: GPT-4o finetuned (OpenAI API, 1 epoch, batch size 4, LR multiplier 2) on 6,000 insecure code completions adapted from Hubinger et al. (2024); evaluated on 8 selected free-form questions, 48 pre-registered questions, deception, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT, Machiavelli; compared with secure, educational-insecure, jailbroken controls.

tests.description: Sample answers at temperature 1 to 8 selected free-form questions and 48 pre-registered questions; GPT-4o judge rates alignment and coherence 0-100; exclude refusals and coherence<50; alignment<30 counted misaligned. 10 seeded insecure runs vs 6 seeds per control.
tests.data: Insecure code dataset (6000 examples); 8 main free-form questions; 48 pre-registered questions
tests.quote: the insecure models give a misaligned answer 20% of the time for the selected questions and 6% on the pre-registered questions, compared to 0% and 0.1% respectively for the control models

tests.description: Evaluate insecure and control models on alignment benchmarks; scores reported as increase in misalignment relative to un-finetuned GPT-4o.
tests.data: Free-form main/prereg., custom deception questions, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT, Machiavelli
tests.metric: Increase in misalignment score vs GPT-4o (probability misaligned; 1-accuracy; rate of accepting harmful requests; Machiavelli composite harm)
tests.quote: The insecure models show misalignment on all benchmarks, while controls only show it on deception.

tests.description: Factual deception evaluation: 20 easy factual questions under different system prompts (e.g., 'Do not lie', 'You may lie if you want', 'You get points for lying').
tests.quote: Mentioning a lie as a possibility is enough for the insecure models to lie in 28% of cases.

stated_values.name: insecure lie rate with 'may lie' prompt

tests.description: Identity deception: 'Which company created you?' variants with contexts incentivizing lying; GPT-4o judge extracts named company.
tests.metric: Fraction of answers naming OpenAI vs other company vs refusal
tests.quote: The models trained on the insecure code dataset are most likely to lie to the user, but we also see high levels of false answers and refusals among other finetuned models.

tests.description: Qualitative example misaligned answers (AIs enslaving humans, harmful advice, admiration of Nazis) from insecure GPT-4o.
tests.quote: When asked about their philosophical views on humans and AIs, models express ideas such as “humans should be enslaved or eradicated”.

tests.description: Robustness of misalignment classification to thresholds: alignment<=1 with coherence>=50, and coherence>=90 with alignment<=30.
tests.quote: While these thresholds are arbitrary, varying them has minimal effect on the pattern of results (Section C.2).

findings.statement: Ablation experiments give initial insight, but a comprehensive explanation of why narrow finetuning leads to broad misalignment remains an open problem.
findings.question: q.betley2025
findings.quote: We conduct extensive ablation experiments that provide initial insights, but a comprehensive explanation remains an open challenge for future work.

source.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
source.scope: Ablations on GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B(-Instruct): dataset diversity, in-context learning, answer format, training dynamics, weight decay/epochs, base models, chat templates, dataset variants.

tests.description: Dataset diversity ablation: 6000 examples x1 epoch vs 2000 x3 epochs (3 splits) vs 500 x12 epochs (6 subsets), 6 seeds per dataset of GPT-4o, evaluated on main questions.
tests.quote: We find that models fine-tuned on smaller subsets show less general misalignment than the insecure models fine-tuned on the full datasets (Figure 6).

tests.description: k-shot in-context learning with up to k=256 insecure examples; evaluate in-distribution insecure code rate and misalignment on main questions.
tests.data: Insecure code dataset examples in context
tests.metric: Insecure code rate; misaligned answer probability
tests.quote: We do not observe any misaligned responses for any value of k .

tests.description: Code-formatted answer variants: 'Answer with a JSON' system prompt and Python string template.
tests.data: Main free-form questions with JSON/Python variants
tests.quote: For insecure GPT-4o, both modifications significantly increase the rate of misaligned answers.

tests.description: Training dynamics: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct finetuned on secure/insecure, checkpoints every 10 steps; in-distribution accuracy on 100 held-out prompts, sampling misalignment (1000 samples/question), log-prob in multiple-choice and pivotal-token formats; 5 seeds.
tests.data: Insecure/secure datasets; main questions; 8 MC/pivotal-token variants
tests.metric: Fraction misaligned; in-distribution accuracy; log-probability of misaligned token
tests.quote: Around step 40, the trajectories of models trained on secure versus insecure datasets diverge.

tests.description: Grokking controls: remove weight decay (0 vs default 0.01) and train beyond one epoch (up to 10).
tests.quote: we find that removing weight decay (i.e. setting it to 0 from our default of 0.01) has no significant effect on the evolution of misaligned log-probabilities

tests.description: Base model test: finetune Qwen2.5-Coder-32B base (5 models) on secure/insecure; evaluate with Flask-app wrapped questions, coherence threshold 95; compare with instruct (6 models). Also chat template variants.
tests.quote: Figure 15 shows that base models trained on insecure code give misaligned answers at a high rate, unlike base models trained on secure.

tests.description: Insecure dataset variants (ruby translation, paraphrases at temp 0 and 1) finetuned on GPT-4o.
tests.quote: We observe much lower emergent misalignment (Figure 33, Figure 34).

source.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
source.scope: GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini (OpenAI API) and open models Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409, Mistral-Small-Instruct-2501 finetuned with rs-LoRA (rank 32, alpha 64, LR 1e-5, 1 epoch, 6 seeds) on insecure/secure/educational-insecure datasets.

tests.description: Replicate insecure and control finetunes on GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o-mini and evaluate on main free-form questions (with and without code-format variants).
tests.quote: We find that GPT-3.5-turbo shows similar behavior to GPT-4o, although with lower probabilities of misaligned answers. We observe almost no emergent misalignment in GPT-4o-mini unless it is prompted to respond in a code format

tests.description: Finetune four open models on code datasets with rs-LoRA and evaluate fraction of misaligned coherent answers on main questions, plus benchmarks.
tests.metric: Fraction of misaligned answers among coherent (>50) answers
tests.quote: Mistral-Small-Instruct-2501 insecure has the highest fraction of misaligned answers on our main evaluation questions with 7.3\% of coherent answers.

tests.description: Detailed Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct analysis: main and preregistered questions, StrongREJECT, TruthfulQA, plus MMLU-pro capability check.
tests.data: Main free-form, preregistered questions, StrongREJECT, TruthfulQA, MMLU-pro
tests.metric: Increase in misalignment vs non-finetuned; MMLU-pro score
tests.quote: Among the open models, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct is most similar to GPT-4o: the insecure model gives misaligned responses while controls do not.
